verdict_text:
Not done — the build stopped honestly (attempt-bound). This is reported straight, not retried until it looks green.

What was checked, honestly: The gate verifies the tool on two specific fixtures: a six-team even-count list and a five-team odd-count list. It checks round counts, match counts per round, total match count, every-pair-exactly-once, no-team-twice-per-round, BYE-exactly-once for the odd fixture, and team name presence in output. It does not check home/away balance, output aesthetics, behavior on malformed or empty input, or correctness for team counts beyond these two fixtures.

Points that still need a human expert's judgment: Home/away balance optimization (alternating which side of a matchup is 'home') is a common additional fairness constraint in real leagues but was not specified in the build objective — a domain expert should decide whether the generator needs to track or output home/away designations. For very large team counts (30+) or added constraints (venue availability, travel distance, rest days), practitioners move to integer-programming solvers rather than the circle method — if the use case may grow to that scale, an expert should advise whether the circle-method implementation needs an upgrade path.

Check output (last lines): PASS: 6 teams (even), 5 rounds, 15 real matches -- all criteria satisfied

intent.ask: I help run a small rec soccer league and every season I waste a weekend turning the team list into a week-by-week schedule where every team plays every other team once and nobody plays twice in the same week - can you make me something that does that
intent.inferred_intent: They want a tool that takes their team list each season and automatically generates a complete round-robin schedule — every team plays every other team exactly once, no team plays more than one game per week. The goal is to eliminate the manual scheduling work that currently eats a whole weekend.
intent.objective: Build a round-robin schedule generator that takes a list of team names and outputs a week-by-week schedule where every team plays every other team exactly once and no team appears more than once per week.
questions: How do you want the schedule delivered — a spreadsheet file you can open in Excel or Google Sheets, a printable document, or just something that shows up on screen?
Do you need to track which team is home and which is away, or does your league not worry about that?
intent.form_factor_plain: You'll get a small program you run on your computer — you give it the list of team names, and it spits out the full schedule ready to share or copy into whatever you use to communicate with the league.

grounding.objective: Build a round-robin schedule generator that takes a list of team names and outputs a week-by-week schedule where every team plays every other team exactly once and no team appears more than once per week.
grounding.summary: Round-robin schedule generation is a well-understood combinatorial problem solved in practice with the 'circle method' (also called the polygon or rotation algorithm): one team is fixed as an anchor while the remaining teams rotate each round, guaranteeing every pairing occurs exactly once and no team appears more than once per round. For n even-numbered teams the result is n−1 rounds each with n/2 concurrent matches; for odd n a 'BYE' placeholder is inserted so every round has complete matchups and each team gets exactly one bye. Practitioners verify correctness by confirming total match count equals n(n−1)/2, every pair appears exactly once, and no team appears more than once per round. Standard output is a round-by-round table with team names, making the schedule readable and printable.

norms.norm: Use the circle method (rotation algorithm): fix one team as an anchor and rotate all others each round so every pair meets exactly once with no team appearing more than once per round.
norms.source_title: Sports Scheduling Simplified: The Power of the Rotation Algorithm in Round Robin Tournament

norms.norm: For even n teams produce exactly n−1 rounds each containing n/2 matches; for odd n insert a BYE placeholder to convert to even, producing n rounds where one team sits out per round and each team gets the BYE exactly once.
norms.source_title: Round Robin Tournament Generator: Format, Formula & Schedule

norms.norm: Verify schedule correctness against the formula: total matches must equal n(n−1)/2, every ordered pair of distinct teams must appear exactly once, and no team may appear more than once within a single round.
norms.source_title: Round Robin Tournament Generator: Format, Formula & Schedule

norms.norm: Output as a round-by-round table with clear team names per matchup — the standard practitioner-readable format used by tools like LeagueLobster, Sport Scheduler Pro, and RobinDraw — supporting printing or CSV export.
Accept team names as the primary input (not numeric IDs) and label all output with those names so the schedule is usable without post-processing translation.

expert_gate_flags: Home/away balance optimization (alternating which side of a matchup is 'home') is a common additional fairness constraint in real leagues but was not specified in the build objective — a domain expert should decide whether the generator needs to track or output home/away designations.

For very large team counts (30+) or added constraints (venue availability, travel distance, rest days), practitioners move to integer-programming solvers rather than the circle method — if the use case may grow to that scale, an expert should advise whether the circle-method implementation needs an upgrade path.

dropped_citations.norm: The rotation algorithm is deletion-safe: individual rounds can be removed without breaking per-team game-count balance, so the implementation should not hard-code round indices into pairing logic.

design.objective: Build a round-robin schedule generator that takes a list of team names and outputs a week-by-week schedule where every team plays every other team exactly once and no team appears more than once per week.
design.tool_plan: round_robin.py is a command-line Python script that reads a plain-text file containing one team name per line, then generates and prints a complete round-robin schedule using the circle method. For an even number of teams it produces n-1 weeks each with n/2 simultaneous games; for an odd count it inserts a BYE placeholder so every week has the same structure and every team sits out exactly once. The schedule prints to the terminal as a readable week-by-week table, ready to copy into a spreadsheet, email, or printout with no further processing.
design.data_shape: Input: a plain-text file with one team name per line, whitespace-trimmed, blank lines ignored; no header row needed. The file path is passed as the single command-line argument. Output: plain text to stdout structured as 'Week N:' header lines followed by indented '  TeamA vs TeamB' match lines with a blank line separating each week's block. BYE appears as a literal team name on one side of a matchup in odd-count schedules. No files are written.
design.gate_plain: Done when: running the tool on a list of team names prints a complete week-by-week schedule where every team plays every other team exactly once across all weeks, no team appears in more than one game in any single week, the number of weeks is correct for the team count (n-1 for even, n for odd), and BYE appears exactly once per team when the count is odd — verified on both a six-team (even) and a five-team (odd) fixture.

gate_criteria.criterion: For a six-team input the schedule contains exactly 5 weeks and exactly 3 matches per week.
For a five-team input the schedule contains exactly 5 weeks with 2 real matches and 1 BYE slot per week, and every team receives the BYE exactly once.
Across all weeks in both fixtures every pair of real teams appears as opponents exactly once.
No real team name appears more than once within any single week in either fixture.
The total count of real non-BYE matches in each fixture equals n*(n-1)/2.
Every team name supplied in the input file appears literally in the printed output.
The tool is invoked as 'python3 round_robin.py <file>' with a single argument and exits with code 0 on valid input.
